definitions.explanation: A polite term to refer to another person's wife.

examples.japanese: {奥|おく}さんは{元気|げんき}ですか。
{田中|たなか}さんの{奥|おく}さん
{奥|おく}さんによろしくお{伝|つた}えください。
examples.english: Please give my regards to your wife.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{奥|おく}さんとよく{話|はな}す。
examples.english: I often talk with the neighbor's wife.

examples.japanese: {山田|やまだ}さんの{奥|おく}さんは{料理|りょうり}がとても{上手|じょうず}で、いつもおいしいものを{作|つく}ってくれる。
examples.english: Mr. Yamada's wife is a very good cook and always makes delicious food for us.

notes:
{奥|おく}さん is a polite term used to refer to someone else's wife. Never use it for your own wife when speaking to others.

WIFE TERMS IN JAPANESE:
- {奥|おく}さん / {奥様|おくさま}: someone else's wife (polite / very polite)
- {妻|つま}: my wife (neutral, most standard)
- {家内|かない}: my wife (humble, traditional — some consider it old-fashioned)
- かみさん: wife (casual, familiar)
- {嫁|よめ}: wife (casual); also means bride or daughter-in-law

ETYMOLOGY:
From {奥|おく} (inner part), originally referring to the person who stays in the inner rooms of the house.

USAGE:
Also used as a form of address for married women in general, similar to 'ma'am': {奥|おく}さん、これ{落|お}としましたよ (Ma'am, you dropped this).
